study type: Multi-centre retrospective cohort study and interrupted time-series analysis
exposure: exposure to the COVID-19 pandemic during pregnancy
cohort: Nulliparous mothers with singleton infants in cephalic presentation at term, born in Melbourne between January 2019 and March 2022, were included.
finding: The study found no significant additional effect of the COVID-19 pandemic on pre-existing upward trends in maternal BMI >= 25 kg/m^2, macrosomia, and caesarean section, despite some rates being higher in the pandemic-exposed cohort.
mod_finding: The increase in the overall caesarean section rate in the pandemic-exposed cohort was specifically confined to individuals undergoing induction of labour or having a pre-labour caesarean section.
